The arm estimates that the worker is farther away. The humanoid does not receive a stop signal as a person crosses its path. In each case, a fault could cause that mismatch. titulo: Researchers develop privacy-friendly, secure and sustainable AI techniques for medical imaging
resumo: Artificial intelligence can be helpful in analyzing medical images and support radiotherapy planning workflows. However, huge amounts of sensitive patient data are needed to train robust AI models. Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) have investigated how hospitals can jointly develop AI models for radiation therapy applications without exchanging such data. In their project, they use federated learning, a process in which a single model is trained at a decentralized location while the data remains in place. Their results demonstrate not only the technical feasibility of the approach but also its safe, more sustainable, and accessible use.

titulo: How the heart's unusual carbohydrate metabolism helps it stay strong

titulo: Microsoft pulls 7 eMudhra certificates from Windows. Here’s what that means
resumo: Yesterday, October 26th, Microsoft released a Windows security update that removes seven certificates associated with Indian company eMudhra. The reason for this is that the private keys for eight intermediate certificates held by eMudhra were recently discovered to be so weak that they could be easily recreated, allowing attackers to forge digital certificates and pose as legitimate websites or applications. Microsoft had previously blocked the affected certificates directly on October 20th, but this new measure goes further by also removing seven certificates higher up in the certificate hierarchy. A similar change is scheduled for Microsoft Edge today, October 27th. For ordinary Windows users, the recommendation is to allow automatic certificate updates and browser updates to run as normal. However, computers without an internet connection or with automatic certificate updates disabled may need to be updated manually. For more details and the next steps, this Microsoft blog post .
